facts.material: flexible insulating substrate with printed copper runs, polyimide insulating coating, gold-plated edge fingers
facts.function: electrical interconnection according to a pre-established conductor pattern
facts.form: flexible printed circuit fitted with two non-printed connectors; no active or other non-printed components

gri_path: GRI 1: chapter 85 note 8 defines printed circuits of heading 8534 as conductor patterns formed on an insulating base by a printing process, and expressly allows them to be fitted with non-printed connecting elements
The two connectors and gold edge fingers are connecting elements, so the assembly remains a printed circuit and does not become a printed circuit assembly of 8473/8517/8538/8543 etc.
Section XVI note 2(a): a part that is a good of heading 8534 is classified in its own heading
GRI 6: 8534.00.00 printed circuits; other; flexible type -> .80

rejected_alternatives.reason: the connectors are only fitted to the printed circuit; the article as a whole is the printed circuit under chapter 85 note 8
no active elements that produce, rectify, modulate or amplify signals
parts provisions do not apply because 8534 describes the good (Section XVI note 2(a))
other rigid circuits; this circuit is of the flexible type

classification.rationale: Chapter 85 note 8 defines printed circuits as conductor patterns formed on an insulating base, and states that they may be fitted with non-printed connecting elements. A flexible substrate with copper runs, polyimide coating, gold edge fingers and two connectors therefore stays in heading 8534. Under Section XVI note 2(a), the parts provisions do not apply. The flexible type line is 8534.00.00.80. NY N325811 (in force) confirms that heading 8534 takes precedence over parts provisions for printed circuit substrates.
